lead.headline: Grimes Drops 47 as Lakers Erase 18-Point Hole
lead.subhead: Down 18 to Charlotte, the Lakers kept swinging. Quentin Grimes poured in a career-high 47 and Los Angeles won 118-114 in overtime, its ninth straight win. A deficit is just the starting line for a comeback.

articles.body: Detroit held San Antonio to 93 and won 105-93, ending the Spurs' 12-game win streak. Somebody has to be the team that stops the run. Be that team today.
Darius Fulghum beat previously unbeaten Diego Pacheco by unanimous decision in a WBA super-middleweight eliminator. Nobody's record is a wall. It's just a number until someone shows up ready.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Wednesday, the day of Mercury: messenger, merchant, quick mind. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Clear the head, then make every word you speak today land.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds squares the mind. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then go build.

mindset.body: The Lakers trailed by 18 and still won in overtime. Grimes didn't wait for permission. He took the shots and hit 47. Midweek is where most people coast. You don't. Make the first call, ask for the next step, close the gap one possession at a time. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Wednesday, the day of Mercury: run this right after Morning Charge. It's about 38° and clear, so keep the RipStick finisher indoors. Quick hands, quick mind: move with snap.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom's RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

items.hed: OpenAI ships GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.body: OpenAI launched two models: Astra for complex professional work and Sol for fast everyday tasks. Both are in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API.

items.hed: Siri AI opens to all developers
items.body: Apple opened its Siri AI Developer Preview in the 27.3 betas. Any app can expose actions through App Intents and teach Siri multi-step 'app skills.' Safari also gained 'Ask About Page.'

items.hed: X pauses training on agent-gathered data
items.body: After Ireland's privacy regulator stepped in, X stopped using third-party data collected by its agents to train AI. Anthropic, meanwhile, rolled out Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2.

Wednesday belongs to Mercury, the Roman Hermes: god of messengers, merchants and crossroads. In Hermetic tradition he rules speech, trade and quick thinking. For a man who sells for a living, it's your planet.
The Emerald Tablet, attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, teaches that what is above mirrors what is below. The inner order you build each morning shows up in the outer results you get by afternoon.

'If you bring forth what is within you, what you bring forth will save you. If you do not bring forth what is within you, what you do not bring forth will destroy you.' Ship the thing you're carrying.

lesson.oneLiner: Small custom apps now start with a clear ask, not a code editor.
beats: Name one annoying repeat task: sorting drop requests, logging leads, tracking a launch checklist.
Write the spec in plain words: what goes in, what comes out, who uses it.
Hand that spec to an assistant and ask for the smallest working version first.
Use it for a week, then ask for one improvement at a time.
lesson.takeaway: A clear spec is the new code.
